props.title: Inception: The Cobol Job
props.initialSlug: Before the dream, there was the job.

sections.content: **Inception: The Cobol Job (2010)** (2010) serves as a fascinating animated prequel to Christopher Nolan's mind-bending masterpiece Inception (2010). This short film bridges crucial narrative gaps, showing how Cobb (DiCaprio) and Arthur first got involved with Cobol Engineering before the events of the main film. It's part of a larger trend of supplementary animated content expanding blockbuster universes, similar to how The Animatrix (2003) deepened the mythology of **The Matrix** (1999).

sections.content: The animation style of **The Cobol Job** (2010) draws from both anime influences and Western animation techniques, following a pattern established by other successful film-to-animation adaptations like **Batman: Gotham Knight** (2008) and **Tales of the Black Freighter** (2009). These projects demonstrate how animation can fill crucial narrative gaps while maintaining the visual sophistication of their live-action counterparts.

What makes **The Cobol Job** particularly significant is how it maintains Nolan's complex approach to time and narrative structure, even in animated form. Like Paprika (2006), which heavily influenced **Inception**, it uses animation to portray dream logic in ways live action simply cannot achieve. SUBHEAD: Bridging Narratives Through Animation

movies.title: Paprika

sections.content: The trend of using animated shorts to expand blockbuster universes gained significant traction in the 2000s. **Final Flight of the Osiris** (2003) connected **The Matrix Reloaded** (2003) to **Enter the Matrix**, while **Blade Runner: Black Out 2022** (2017) bridged the 30-year gap between **Blade Runner** (1982) and **Blade Runner 2049** (2017).
